# 02 Give the flowchart node frame its own class

## Outcome

A flowchart node's rect carries `siren-node-frame`, and the theme styles it directly, exactly as
the class diagram's `siren-class-frame` already works.

## Why this ticket exists

`renderToSVG` puts `siren-node` on the enclosing `<g>` and nothing on the `<rect>`; the theme
reaches it with the descendant selector `.siren-node rect`. The class diagram does the opposite —
`.siren-class-frame` on the rect, selected directly — and ADR-0008's placement argument is written
in those terms: an author's declaration must land on the element the theme styles directly, because
a directly-applied declaration beats an inherited one.

The next ticket puts an inline style on that rect. It works either way, but the two kinds would
read differently for no reason an author or a maintainer could see. Doing it first, alone, keeps
the tracer ticket about styling rather than about renaming.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The `<rect>` inside `<g class="siren-node">` carries `class="siren-node-frame"`.
- [x] `theme/default.css` selects `.siren-node-frame` directly instead of `.siren-node rect`, and
      `.siren-node text` likewise gains a directly-selected class if the same argument applies to
      it — check whether it does and say so, rather than changing it reflexively.
- [x] Rendering is otherwise unchanged: every existing `renderToSVG.test.ts` and `index.test.ts`
      assertion about node geometry, ids and animation classes passes untouched.
- [x] The theme's own tests still pass. `theme/default.test.ts` is in your write scope only if it
      asserts the old selector.
- [x] A comment in `default.css` records that this class exists so an author style can land
      directly on it (ADR-0008), not merely as a naming tidy-up.
- [x] This is a public CSS surface change. Note in your report whether a consumer's existing
      `.siren-node rect` rule still works — verify it, do not assume.

## Test seam

`render()` and `renderToSVG` for the emitted class; `theme/default.test.ts` for the selector.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/src/renderer/renderToSVG.ts`
- `packages/core/src/renderer/renderToSVG.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/theme/default.css`
- `packages/core/src/theme/default.test.ts`

Do **not** touch `contracts.ts` or anything under `graph-model/` — ticket 01 owns those this round.
